picks.style: ancient greek hymn, lyre and aulos, single male voice over drone, processional, reverent, unhurried
picks.why: The invocation and the meadow of narcissus at which heaven, earth and sea laughed for joy.

picks.style: ancient dramatic hymn, frame drum and low aulos, urgent male voice, dark, propulsive
picks.why: The earth yawns, Hades springs out, and the girl's cry is heard by no one but Hecate and the Sun.

picks.style: mystery-rite chant, deep drone, layered voices, torchlit, slow, initiatory
picks.why: The Eleusinian blessing — happy is he who has seen these mysteries — the hymn's most quoted lines.

picks.style: winter sea lament, bowed strings and low whistle, cold male voice, stark, shivering, slow
picks.why: The fisher's frozen night against the soft beds of the town — a complete, bitter contrast.

picks.style: baroque sea eclogue, viol consort and recorder, plaintive tenor, rolling, wistful
picks.why: The rainbow arch drinking up the sea, turned into a warning that beauty is as quickly gone.

picks.style: english pastoral air, harpsichord and cello, wry warm baritone, steady, homely
picks.why: The lobster carried off who finds his own rock again — the love of country is not confined to man.

picks.style: sacred anthem, chapel organ and choir, high trebles over full voices, radiant, building
picks.why: The tuneful planets and cherubim singing holy, holy, holy — built for a choir.

picks.style: english ode, chamber strings and continuo, troubled tenor, restless, nocturnal
picks.why: Sleepless on the bed with thoughts like hornets, asking whether goodness gets any reward.

picks.style: ode to music, lute and strings, rapt soprano, flowing, luminous
picks.why: Sappho's lute complaining and Anacreon's honeyed tongue — a vision made entirely of sound.

picks.style: english pastoral ballad, guitar and flute, plaintive female voice, lilting, simple
picks.why: A true ballad opening: the ribbons bought at the fair for Phillis, the nymph that I hate.

picks.style: folk hymn, acoustic guitar, warm female vocal, unhurried, contented
picks.why: The Wish — a cottage far from ball and masquerade, ending life without a tear.

picks.style: spring carol with refrain, fiddle and tambourine, bright soprano with small chorus, buoyant
picks.why: Every stanza closes on hail, genial goddess of the blooming spring — a built-in refrain.

picks.style: georgian ballad, harpsichord and flute, light tenor, tripping anapests, playful
picks.why: Meeting the god of Love by the stream, who sorts his arrows by the bird each feather came from.

picks.style: elegiac air, viola and fortepiano, mournful soprano, slow, resigned
picks.why: The drooping sunflower and trailing woodbine, closing on the epitaph — Iris loved Philus, and she died sincere.

picks.style: roman tragic declamation, timpani and low strings, dramatic bass, stormy, surging
picks.why: Only candidate; the quoted storm — the sea bristles, the sky trembles, the winds burst forth — is real verse.

picks.style: german revolutionary ballad, marching drum and accordion, gritty male chorus, defiant, grim, driving
picks.why: Only candidate; the barricade dead calling the king down to bare his head — a full, ferocious stanza.

picks.style: irish protest ballad, bodhran and fiddle, stern male voice, driving, defiant
picks.why: Only candidate, but a complete quatrain of curse with real force.
